newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close at record high after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close at record high after U.S. data.

text.p: French stocks rose to close at a record high on Tuesday, boosted by market-friendly U.S. economic data which lowered fears of a U.S. interest rate hike and lifted debt markets in the United States and Europe.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 47.59 points or 1.95 percent at 2,482.76, breaking the old record of 2,461.25 set on January 23.
Shortly after the close, the CAC-40 futures contract was up two points at 2,483.
Volume was a heavy 8.95 billion francs.
The release of the U.S. employment cost index for the fourth quarter, which showed the cost of labour rose a smaller than expected 0.8 percent, was the main cause for the bourse's rise.

Analysts in the United States had said before the index's release that a stronger-than-expected result could trigger a hike in short term U.S. interest rates. A weaker-than-expected index showed labor cost, a key determinant of inflation, were not in danger of getting out of control and lowered the chance of a rise in U.S. rates, they said.
The dollar's continued strong performance against European currencies also helped the bourse, dealers said.

"Although wages have picked up a little bit, overall compensation, which is what matters, is rising barely steadily at three percent," said James Glassman, senior economist at Chase in New York. "I think this is pretty good news."
The market's eyes will now turn to U.S. durable goods data for December, due Wednesday, and the U.S. Federal Reserve's next policy setting meeting, set for February 4 and 5, dealers said.
* Moulinex ends 8.52 percent higher at 142.60 francs after earlier being suspended limit up. The share rose after the company predicted improved operating earnings.
* Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux both rise as rumours of a linkup, last floated in 1995, resurfaced. Suez also gains from saying on Monday it would post a 1996 profit.
Suez ends day 6.94 percent higher at 248 francs and Lyonnaise finishes 5.05 percent higher at 562 francs.
"Considered several times and regularly postponed, the last time in 1995, this operation is once again under review," daily Le Figaro said, citing sources close to the affair.
Suez and Lyonnaise spokeswomen said the groups' policy was not to comment on "rumours". Suez said on Monday it would earn net profit of about 800 million francs in 1996.
*Elf Aquitaine and 55-percent owned unit Sanofi both higher after a source close to the company said Sanofi was seeking one or two partners to double its size and help it meet development costs.
Sanofi ended 3.48 percent higher at 565 francs while Elf was up 5.46 percent at 541 france.

* Bic ends up 1.37 percent at 891 francs, Valeo closes up 3.24 percent at 363.50 francs and AGF finishes up 4.83 percent at 173.80 francs, all due to being named members of CAC-40 index, replacing UAP, Eurotunnel and Saint Louis.
* UAP closes down 0.57 percent at 142.30 francs, Eurotunnel ends off 0.67 percent at 7.45 francs and Saint Louis drops 2.53 percent at 1,386 francs, all as a result of the change.
